newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq papers herald partial oil exports as victory.
newsitem.headline: Iraq papers herald partial oil exports as victory.

text.p: State-run newspapers said on Wednesday that the resumption of oil exports by Iraq was a victory over U.S. persistence to keep sanctions on Baghdad intact.
"The will of the steadfast and patient Iraq triumphed and all U.S. obstacles have gone in vain," said the ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra in a front-page editorial.
It said allowing partial exports of $2 billion over six months was not out of humanitarian concerns for the Iraqi people, as depicted by "political leaders (U.S.) who wanted to destroy our land.
"It (oil flow) came as a result of other factors, namely...the wisdom of the historic leadership of President Saddam Hussein," Thawra said.
Other newspapers said the flow of Iraqi crude marked the start of the process to dismantle the wall of sanctions against Iraq.
"The embargo has cracked," said the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya in a banner headline.
There was no comment from Iraq on reports that oil from Kirkuk had not yet reached Turkey due to technical failures on the Iraqi side of the twin pipeline through Turkish territory.
Saddam pressed the button to start Iraqi oil flowing to world markets on Tuesday for the first time since 1990, when U.N. sanctions were imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait.
